replication.target_description: Broad mental-fatigue/physical-performance description; no replication locator. Candidate paired-condition outcomes: cycling time-to-exhaustion, average cycling heart rate and session RPE; exact intended test is unresolved.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text begins with the title Does mental fatigue impair physical performance? A replication study and names Darías Holgado, Esther Troya, José C. Perales, Miguel A. Vadillo and Daniel Sanabria, matching the neutral replication reference. It is a full 17-page empirical manuscript with Methods, Results, Discussion and references, not an abstract, secondary article or preregistration. It identifies the data project https://osf.io/wqkap/ and preregistered protocol https://osf.io/7hz3x. The text metadata names https://osf.io/download/5qjxs/; the supplied DOI 10.31236/osf.io/tzn6d is not printed, and the exact version/year cannot be independently confirmed from this cache. References include a 2020 paper, so this may be a later manuscript version than the 2019 neutral citation. No PDF was supplied. Only es_value_r and pval_value_r assigned. The replication description and absent locator do not specify which of the three listed dependent variables is intended. Do not select by row order or requested numeric metric. Printed candidates: time-to-exhaustion BF01 = 9.762; average heart rate during cycling BF01 = 2.587; session RPE BF01 = 2.902. All are one-sided Bayes factors, not Cohen d. The report provides condition means/uncertainty and Bayesian evidence, with no same-test frequentist p in these result paragraphs. No conversion performed. Original, replication n and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
